name: ENMAG survey
description: Global society faces the critical challenges of eradicating poverty, ensuring food security, and addressing environmental degradation. In this context, agricultural microbusinesses emerge as essential actors in productive dynamics, contributing significantly to food sovereignty and economic transformation. In Latin America, family farming supplies 53% of global food demand, accounts for 7.92% of GDP, and employs one-fifth of the economically active population. However, many microbusinesses operate empirically and face severe technical, infrastructural, and financial limitations. In Ecuador, private initiatives incorporate sustainable practices such as crop rotation, the use of organic inputs, the recovery of ancestral knowledge, and efficient community water management. However, these practices have not been systematically evaluated due to a lack of assessment instruments adapted to small-scale agricultural activities. This study aims to design a validation instrument with standardized sustainability indicators adapted to the local contexts of agricultural microbusinesses. The instrument goes beyond traditional environmental and economic metrics by integrating social and cultural dimensions that are essential for a comprehensive assessment of sustainability. The research employed the Framework for the Evaluation of Natural Resource Management Systems (MESMIS Framework) to design the ENMAG survey (Survey for Agricultural Microbusinesses).
